title: Solar lentigines
summary: Benign sun-induced lentigines versus freckles, melasma and seborrhoeic keratoses — with lentigo maligna as the red-flag differential.

glance.think: Flat, evenly brown macules on the face or backs of the hands of an older outdoor worker that do not fade in winter.
glance.engine: Chronic UV increases local melanocyte number and activity along elongated rete ridges.
glance.backbone: Photoprotection forever; topical retinoids/azelaic acid for modest fading; cryotherapy/IPL/laser only after cancer exclusion — usually private.
glance.never_miss: Irregular, multicoloured, enlarging facial pigment → lentigo maligna — urgent suspected-cancer referral. Never laser an undiagnosed pigmented lesion.

what: **Solar lentigines** (“age spots”, “liver spots”) are benign flat tan-to-dark-brown macules on chronically sun-exposed skin. They mark cumulative UV damage and skin-cancer risk but are not themselves premalignant.
cause: UV-driven localised melanocyte hyperactivity. Risk rises with fair skin, outdoor work, sunburn history, sunbeds and age.

list: Uniform light-to-dark brown macules with a regular border; face, dorsal hands, forearms, shoulders.
May coexist with AK field change and photoageing.

diagnosis: Clinical ± dermoscopy (fingerprint/moth-eaten border patterns). Biopsy or refer asymmetric, irregular, enlarging, ugly-duckling or grey-regression lesions — especially on the face.

head: Look-alike
Clues
rows: Symmetrical patches; hormones; worsened by heat/IPL — see [melasma](condition:melasma-facial-melanosis)
Irregular colours, slow enlargement on older face → NG12 referral

list: Daily broad-spectrum SPF 30–50 (± tinted); hats/gloves for driving and gardening — without this, treated lesions return.
Examine the whole photodamaged field for AK/BCC/SCC/lentigo maligna.
Modest topicals: retinoids, azelaic acid; short specialist hydroquinone courses only (ochronosis risk).
Procedural (usually private): light cryotherapy (hypopigmentation risk, especially in darker skin), pigment laser for discrete spots, IPL for diffuse pigment+redness — only after diagnosis is secure.
Melasma is a poor IPL indication and can worsen.

red_flags: Any lesion suspicious for lentigo maligna or melanoma → urgent suspected-cancer pathway.
Do not treat undiagnosed pigment with cryotherapy, IPL or laser.
pearls: Solar lentigines are a UV dosimeter — use the visit for skin-cancer education.
Hand spots are a classic patient question; same rules as the face.

Flat brown marks that become raised and warty are usually [seborrhoeic keratoses](condition:seborrhoeic-keratosis); a lentigo that darkens or spreads unevenly on the face may be [lentigo maligna](condition:melanoma).
